subject: Mathematics
objective: Connect a point on the unit circle to the height of the sine curve.
learner: Knows right-triangle ratios; has not connected circular motion to sine.
expectedBehavior: A corresponding sine point or height changes
Angle and sine height are visibly linked
misconceptions: Sine is only a triangle ratio
The sine value is the x-coordinate
requiredInteraction: The learner must be able to change the angle or step through it.
correctnessCriteria: At 0 and pi the sine height is 0
At pi/2 the height is maximal
The displayed y-coordinate and sine value agree
accessibility: alt text; keyboard-operable controls; no essential meaning only by color

subject: Mathematics
objective: Let a learner who knows algebra but not calculus see why a step goes opposite the gradient.
expectedBehavior: Show a current point and a descent direction
A parameter changes the step and its effect
The relationship between slope and direction is visible
misconceptions: A larger learning rate is always better
The gradient points downhill
requiredInteraction: Learner changes a learning-rate-like parameter or steps the update.
correctnessCriteria: Step direction opposes the local gradient
The step is scaled by the parameter
No claim that a bigger step always converges
accessibility: alt text; keyboard-operable controls; reduced-motion fallback

subject: Mathematics
objective: Show a tangent line whose slope matches the derivative at a movable point.
learner: Can read coordinates on a graph.
expectedBehavior: A point moves along a curve
Slope is shown as rise/run or a sign
misconceptions: Derivative is the value of the function
A positive derivative means the function is positive
requiredInteraction: Move the point or step through positions.
correctnessCriteria: Tangent slope matches the function's local slope
Sign of slope matches whether the function is rising
No false claim about non-differentiable points
accessibility: figure alt; keyboard control; avoid color-only sign

subject: Mathematics
objective: Show how a matrix maps basis vectors and a shape in the plane.
learner: Has seen vectors but not matrix geometry.
expectedBehavior: Basis vectors move to transformed positions
Matrix entries are linked to visible changes
misconceptions: Matrix multiplication is just elementwise multiplication
The transformed grid is unchanged
requiredInteraction: Change one matrix entry or pick a preset.
correctnessCriteria: Transformed basis vectors match matrix columns
Shape coordinates transform consistently
Determinant/area warning only if computed correctly
accessibility: alt; keyboard controls; no essential meaning by color

subject: Mathematics
objective: Show g(x) then f(g(x)) as a two-stage machine or graph mapping.
expectedBehavior: Input passes through two stages in order
Intermediate value and final value are distinguishable
Changing order changes the result when appropriate
misconceptions: f(g(x)) always equals g(f(x))
Composition is multiplication of outputs
requiredInteraction: Change x or swap/compare the two stages.
correctnessCriteria: Intermediate value is g(x)
Final value is f(g(x))
No commutativity claim unless the specific functions commute

subject: Physics
objective: Show how launch angle changes the trajectory at a fixed speed.
expectedBehavior: Maximum height and range are visible
The paired angles with equal range can be compared
misconceptions: 45 degrees always gives the maximum range regardless of launch height
Horizontal speed changes the vertical acceleration
requiredInteraction: Change the launch angle and replay.
correctnessCriteria: Trajectory follows consistent projectile kinematics
45 degrees maximizes range for equal launch and landing heights
No false dependence of a downward direction on horizontal speed
accessibility: alt; keyboard; do not rely solely on color

subject: Physics
objective: Show how length and initial release angle affect the period of a pendulum.
expectedBehavior: Length or angle changes the motion
misconceptions: Pendulum period depends strongly on mass
The small-angle approximation is exact at all angles
requiredInteraction: Change length or release angle and replay.
correctnessCriteria: Longer length gives a longer period in the model
Small-angle behavior is not presented as exact for large angles
Mass is not falsely shown as the main period driver

subject: Physics
objective: Show how gravity components change with incline angle.
learner: Knows forces as pushes and pulls.
expectedBehavior: Gravity component along the plane changes
Angle is visibly connected to components
misconceptions: Normal force equals weight at every angle
Friction is always equal to weight
requiredInteraction: Change the incline angle.
correctnessCriteria: Along-plane component scales with sin(theta)
Normal component scales with cos(theta)
Component directions are correct

subject: Physics
objective: Show constructive and destructive interference as two waves combine.
misconceptions: Waves cancel by destroying energy
Interference means the waves stop existing
requiredInteraction: Change phase or distance between sources.
correctnessCriteria: In-phase waves add
Opposite-phase waves cancel at the observed point
Energy language is not false

subject: Physics
objective: Show the electric field of one or two point charges as direction and magnitude.
learner: Knows positive and negative charge attracts/repels.
expectedBehavior: Field vectors point away/toward appropriate charges
misconceptions: Field is the same as force on every test charge
Field lines cross
requiredInteraction: Move a test point or change a charge sign.
correctnessCriteria: Field direction for positive/negative charges is correct
Magnitude decreases with distance
No field-line crossing

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show adjacent swaps and the growing sorted suffix.
expectedBehavior: Adjacent pair comparison moves along array
misconceptions: One pass always sorts the whole array
Bubble sort starts from the middle
requiredInteraction: Step or play through comparisons.
correctnessCriteria: Every swap fixes an adjacent inversion
Largest remaining value moves right each pass
Number of comparisons is plausible

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show the interval shrinking and why a sorted array is required.
expectedBehavior: The discarded half is visibly excluded
The search result index is correct
misconceptions: Binary search works on any array
The midpoint is always the answer
requiredInteraction: Choose a target or step through comparisons.
correctnessCriteria: Interval always contains the target if present
Comparison direction matches target vs midpoint
Termination condition is shown
accessibility: alt; keyboard; no color-only half distinction

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show the call stack growing and unwinding for a recursive function.
misconceptions: Recursion runs all calls simultaneously
The base case is executed first
requiredInteraction: Step forward and backward through calls.
correctnessCriteria: LIFO order is correct
Base case is reached
Return values unwind correctly

subject: Computer Science
objective: Contrast LIFO and FIFO operations with the same sequence.
expectedBehavior: Push/pop on a stack vs enqueue/dequeue on a queue
Order of removal is visibly different
misconceptions: Stacks and queues are the same structure
The first inserted item is always removed first
requiredInteraction: Perform or step through operations on both structures.
correctnessCriteria: Stack removes the most recent item
Queue removes the oldest item
No state corruption

subject: Computer Science
objective: Show BFS/DFS visiting order and frontier differences.
misconceptions: DFS always finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph
Visited nodes can be revisited forever
requiredInteraction: Step through traversal and optionally switch BFS/DFS.
correctnessCriteria: Each node is visited once
BFS uses a queue and DFS a stack
BFS gives shortest unweighted path distances when shown
accessibility: alt; keyboard; node labels, not color only

subject: Economics
objective: Show equilibrium where supply and demand curves intersect.
learner: Can read a simple x-y graph.
misconceptions: A price change shifts the demand curve
Equilibrium means everyone can buy at any price
requiredInteraction: Shift supply or demand and observe equilibrium.
correctnessCriteria: Demand slopes down and supply up in the simple model
Intersection is the equilibrium pair
A curve shift is distinguished from movement along a curve

subject: Economics
objective: Show a binding price ceiling producing shortage.
misconceptions: A ceiling always helps buyers
Shortage equals zero supply
requiredInteraction: Move the ceiling price.
correctnessCriteria: Binding only when below equilibrium
Shortage = quantity demanded - quantity supplied
No claim that price controls raise total surplus

subject: Economics
objective: Show opportunity costs and gains from specialization.
expectedBehavior: Each producer's opportunity cost is visible
Terms of trade can be compared
misconceptions: Absolute advantage determines gains from trade
One country must lose in every trade
requiredInteraction: Change production allocation or compare opportunity costs.
correctnessCriteria: Opportunity costs are computed consistently
Specialization increases total output when comparative advantage exists
No false claim of guaranteed equal gains

subject: Statistics
objective: Show sample means varying around a population mean and shrinking spread with n.
expectedBehavior: Population and sampling distribution are distinguished
misconceptions: A larger sample makes each observation closer to the mean
The sampling distribution is the population distribution
requiredInteraction: Change sample size or draw another sample.
correctnessCriteria: Means center near the population mean
Spread decreases with larger n
Individual observations are not confused with sample means

subject: Statistics
objective: Show sums/means of non-normal variables approaching a bell shape.
expectedBehavior: Distribution of means changes with n
Shape approaches bell as n grows
misconceptions: The original data becomes normal
CLT needs normal data to start
requiredInteraction: Change n and resample.
correctnessCriteria: Sampling distribution of means centers near population mean
Spread narrows with n
No claim that raw data turned normal
